Campaign with the strongest business impact

The Rare Tour / Three Courses, Six Hands

Brand & Period

Meatguy Steakhouse / February 2025

Objective & Challenge

Build awareness and reservations for an exclusive chef collaboration at Meatguy Steakhouse.

Audience & My Role

Premium diners and steak enthusiasts, with an exclusive three-course experience as the key proposition. My task was to fill reservations through effective marketing and creative strategy.

Read campaign strategy & creative concept
Winning Campaign 01

Campaign Strategy & Creative Concept

Audience Insight

Many Indonesian diners were unfamiliar with the event and why they should attend. The event’s reputation alone would not secure reservations. Guests needed to understand the experience and what justified the price. Its main attraction was an exclusive menu available only at this event, cooked by guest chefs from a renowned steakhouse in Mexico.

Key Message

A rare opportunity to enjoy an exclusive event menu, prepared by guest chefs from a renowned Mexican steakhouse alongside the Meatguy team.

Hook & Storytelling

Exclusive dishes, cooked by guest chefs from Mexico with Meatguy.
“3 Courses, 6 Hands.”
Three chefs. Three courses. One occasion.

30 days before: teasers, posters, and daily educational content.
21–14 days before: chef introductions and menu previews.
Approaching the final week: Instagram and TikTok teasers supported by Meta Ads.
Final week to event day: countdowns, preparations, and reservation calls to action.

Creative Concept

“3 Courses, 6 Hands, a One-Time Dining Experience.”
Follow three chefs as they create three exclusive dishes, from introductions and preparation to live service at Meatguy. Each piece of content reveals a new detail, turning curiosity into a desire to attend.

Why This Approach

The main barrier was an unclear understanding of the event’s value. A phased educational rollout and the “3 Courses, 6 Hands” hook introduced the chef collaboration and exclusive menu, giving diners a clear reason to reserve.

Distribution Channels

Instagram, TikTok, Meta Ads

Winning Campaign 01

The Rare Tour / Results

IDR 905,647,200Revenue across three days
558Guests / reservations across three days
10.91×Event revenue / marketing spend
24.48%Share of February 2025 revenue
Read results, measurement & learnings

Marketing Investment & Reported Return

Marketing spend: IDR 83,000,000.
Source-reported ROAS / ROI: 10.91× / 990.05%. These figures compare event revenue with marketing spend and do not establish profit ROI or ad-attributed revenue.

What Worked

The campaign recorded approximately IDR 905 million in revenue and 558 guests, contributing 24.48% of Meatguy’s total February 2025 revenue. The event supported reservations and made a significant contribution to the month’s revenue.

Next Optimisation

Focus on content that generates reservation intent, retarget interested audiences, and track reservation sources so each channel’s contribution can be measured and budget allocated more effectively.

Bone Marrow

Meat Explained with the Executive Chef

Read creative approach

What the Creative Shows

The shooting and editing aim for a natural, appetising presentation, allowing the audience to enjoy each visual detail.

My Interpretation

Large cuts of beef or appetising dishes provide an immediate visual hook. The videos combine striking food visuals with authentic cooking processes to reflect the audience’s interest in natural preparation.

Performance Analysis

Creative Performance Comparison

Objective: highlight and upsell menu items.
Comparison period: 15 days.

CreativeViewsRetentionEngagementDistributionReported Result
Tartare on Pavé4.6M73%583OrganicSales increase up to 4%
Bone Marrow3.3M81%734OrganicSales increase up to 14%
Meat Explained1.8M63%903OrganicSales increase up to 25%

Conclusion

Meat Explained showed the strongest reported upselling result, with a sales increase of up to 25% despite fewer views. Prioritise menu education, supported by Tartare on Pavé for reach and Bone Marrow for attention retention.

Historical comparison reported in the portfolio. Observed sales changes do not independently establish causal attribution.

A Real Problem-Solving Example

Situation

Guest numbers declined ahead of an event. We needed an appropriate marketing and creative response to increase reservations and renew audience interest.

My Action

With Threads gaining attention, I used the platform as part of a two-day effort to increase guest numbers. I directed the team to develop a visually engaging creative concept and increased the Meta Ads budget.

Result

Guest numbers increased from 13 to 56 overnight. Most guests arrived as walk-ins rather than through reservations.

Dims The Meatguy / Creative Execution

From First Idea to Final Frame

A clear workflow keeps the creative strong, the production efficient, and the output consistent.

01 / Ideate

Evaluate previous content to identify effective approaches, find new ideas, and understand audience needs and current algorithm trends.

02 / Pre-produce

After evaluation, prepare the script, storyboard, and props required for production.

03 / Produce

Shoot according to the planned script and storyboard to achieve the intended visuals.

04 / Post-produce

Assemble the footage through editing and post-production, following the original concept and objectives.

05 / Deliver

Prepare captions, publish the content, and monitor views to evaluate effectiveness and inform future creative strategy.
